text:
katie: Hey team — FirmGround SI reported failures during on‑prem install this morning, flagged by field eng at 04:12 UTC. Can we do a quick architecture sync?
raj: Seen the thread. What failure are they hitting exactly?
katie: Installer logs show repeated driver init errors on the NIC/GPU side. Saw this in the agent logs:
```
ERROR: failed to register nvidia_uvm: -22
kernel: module nvidia_uvm: disagrees about version of symbol nv_kref_get
```
mohit: That looks like a kernel/module mismatch — probably their AMI was built with an older kernel than the driver binary in the marketplace image.
esme: Do they have a custom kernel/package repo? SI said they patch the base image for compliance.
katie: Yes, they run a hardened reposync job with backported patches. They claimed they used our marketplace image as a base.
raj: Two possibilities: 1) SI rebuilt the image and accidentally mixed driver versions, or 2) our image includes a driver tied to a kernel we didn't pin.
mohit: Quick check — can they run `uname -r` and `modinfo nvidia`? If `modinfo` fails or shows different vermagic, that's the mismatch.
katie: Asking them to run those now. Also, we hit a deployment abort in our installer — stack: `agent -> runtime -> driver probe -> abort`.
jordan: @katie can you confirm the marketplace image digest they pulled? Need the SHA to correlate with our image build matrix.
@katie: I asked for the image sha and kernel output. SI responded with: `image: redwood/edge:3.7.2` (no sha), `uname -r: 5.15.0-58-generic`, `modinfo` threw the vermagic error.
esme: Without the digest we can't be sure which build they used. We should recommend they pull by digest for reproducibility.
mohit: Short term mitigation: tell them to load a driver package matching their kernel (apt/apt-get install --reinstall nvidia-driver-xxx) or rollback to the marketplace image we publish (use digest). Long term: we need better guidance in the SI runbook for kernel-driver compatibility.
katie: SI is on a tight cutover window this week — they want a rollback plan. Also worried about telemetry not reaching us post-install.
raj: Action items: 1) Ask SI to capture image sha + `uname -r` + `modinfo nvidia` (they're doing). 2) If mismatch confirmed, recommend driver reinstall or rebase to published image digest. 3) Partnerships to supply signed image digest link and one‑click rollback doc.
jordan: I'll prepare a short 'rollback by digest' snippet and a signed digest URL to share with SI.
mohit: I'll draft the kernel/driver troubleshooting steps for the runbook and add exact commands.
esme: I'll offer the hosted fallback plan (proxy traffic to hosted Redwood API for inference) so their app doesn't go fully offline while drivers are fixed. Need approvals from security for that path.
katie: Deploy-bot ping — can we also gather installer telemetry logs? We have a missing trace id in their report.
deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] New installer failure event for customer firmground (incident 2026-03-21-0421). Trace ID: missing -> please include `RW_TRACE_ID` in future uploads.
katie: Noted. SI says they didn't set RW_TRACE_ID in their env. I'll ask them to re-run with it so we can pull the trace from our console.
raj: Heads up — coordinate with marketplace team to check the image build matrix. @jordan can you loop them in?
jordan: Will do, looping @marketplace-build. Also adding a note for image signing verification step in the SI handoff doc.
katie: Good. Timeline: SI will try driver reinstall now and report back in ~2h. If that fails, we'll guide rollback to digest and enable hosted fallback.
esme: 👍 please paste the commands you'll send so I can pre-clear the hosted fallback with security.
katie: Copying proposed commands:
```
# check kernel and nvidia module
uname -r
modinfo nvidia || dmesg | tail -n 50
# reinstall matching driver (example)
sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install --reinstall nvidia-driver-525
# or rollback to published image by digest
docker pull redwood/edge@sha256:<digest>
```
katie: I'll post updates here when SI reports back. Thanks all. :pray:
